subject: chemistry
title: Sigma and pi bonds and hybridisation
key_idea: A sigma bond forms by direct overlap of orbitals along the line between two nuclei. A pi bond forms by sideways overlap of p orbitals above and below that line. Mixing s and p orbitals gives sp³, sp² and sp hybrid orbitals, which set the shape round an atom.

blocks.text: Covalent bonds form when atomic orbitals overlap. This section covers the two ways that overlap can happen.

items.meaning: A bond formed by the direct, end-on overlap of orbitals between the bonding atoms.
A bond formed by the sideways overlap of adjacent p orbitals, above and below the σ bond.

items: Every single bond is one σ bond.
A double bond is one σ bond and one π bond.
A triple bond is one σ bond and two π bonds.
A π bond has electron density above and below the line between the nuclei, not along it.
Sideways overlap is weaker than direct overlap, so a π bond is easier to break than a σ bond.

blocks.text: How the bonds form in these molecules

items: **H₂:** the two 1s orbitals overlap directly to form one σ bond.
**C₂H₆:** each C–H σ bond is an sp³ orbital overlapping an s orbital. The C–C σ bond is two sp³ orbitals overlapping directly.
**C₂H₄:** the C=C σ bond is two sp² orbitals overlapping directly. The π bond is the sideways overlap of the two unhybridised p orbitals.
**HCN:** the C–H and C≡N σ bonds use sp orbitals on carbon. The two π bonds are two sideways overlaps of p orbitals, at right angles to each other.
**N₂:** one σ bond from direct overlap, and two π bonds from sideways overlap of p orbitals at right angles.
σ bonds are direct overlap. π bonds are sideways overlap of p orbitals.
A double bond is one σ and one π. A triple bond is one σ and two π.

blocks.text: Hybridisation mixes s and p orbitals into new orbitals of equal energy. This section covers the three types and the shapes they give.

items: In sp³ hybridisation all four orbitals form σ bonds.
In sp² hybridisation the three hybrid orbitals form σ bonds. The remaining unhybridised p orbital overlaps sideways to form a π bond.
In sp hybridisation the two hybrid orbitals form σ bonds. Two unhybridised p orbitals form two π bonds.
In ethene the six atoms all lie in the same flat plane, so the molecule is **planar**. The π bond stops the C=C bond rotating.

diagram.prompt: What is the hybridisation of the carbon atom?

items.text: C in the carbonyl group, C=O, of propanone

items: The number of σ bonds plus lone pairs gives the hybridisation: four is sp³, three is sp² and two is sp.
sp³ is tetrahedral, sp² is trigonal planar and sp is linear.
π bonds are formed only from unhybridised p orbitals.

checks.q: State how the σ and π bonds in a C=C double bond are formed.
checks.a: The σ bond is formed by direct overlap of orbitals between the carbon atoms. The π bond is formed by sideways overlap of adjacent p orbitals above and below the σ bond.

checks.q: State the number of σ bonds and π bonds in HCN, and the hybridisation of the carbon atom.
checks.a: Two σ bonds and two π bonds. The carbon atom is sp hybridised.

checks.q: Explain why ethene is planar and has bond angles of about 120°.
checks.a: Each carbon atom is sp² hybridised and forms three σ bonds, which are trigonal planar at 120°. The unhybridised p orbitals overlap sideways to form the π bond, which holds the atoms in one plane.
